ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached image shows a geometric figure: D, F, G are on the same slanted line, and the ray from F through G is an extension of side DF of triangle DFE. The base of triangle DFE is DE, and the vertex is F. The base angle ∠FDE is labeled 5x°, and the base angle ∠DEF is also labeled 5x°. At point F, the exterior angle ∠EFG formed by ray FG and segment FE is labeled (9x + 7)°. Reasoning: Because ∠EFG is the exterior angle of triangle DFE at point F, according to the triangle exterior angle theorem, the exterior angle is equal to the sum of the two non-adjacent interior angles. So m∠EFG = 5x + 5x = 10x. At the same time, the figure gives m∠EFG = 9x + 7. Therefore 9x + 7 = 10x, solving gives x = 7. Substitute into the exterior angle expression: m∠EFG = 9(7) + 7 = 63 + 7 = 70°.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as triangle DFE with D, F, and G collinear, where ray FG is the extension of side FD. The two base interior angles at D and E are each labeled 5x°, and the exterior angle at F, angle EFG, is labeled (9x+7)°. Use the exterior angle theorem: an exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles. Thus m∠EFG = 5x + 5x = 10x, and also m∠EFG = 9x + 7. Set 9x + 7 = 10x to get x = 7, then compute m∠EFG = 9(7)+7 = 70°.
